title: Intimate partner violence declared an epidemic
subtitle: Paramedic 2024 pre-budget, anti-harassment by-law amendment, housing investment plan, chronic homelessness plan and affordable housing incentives.
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that Regional Council declare intimate partner violence and violence against women an epidemic {{vote:m7}}. The motion also asks the Province to make the same declaration, adds the issue as a separate priority in the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan, and names violence against Indigenous women, girls and 2SLGBTQQIA people. Local agencies said the declaration costs nothing but signals support for survivors.

The committee also recommended amending the Code of Use by-law to prohibit harassing and discriminatory behaviour on Regional premises. It added socio-economic and housing status to the protected grounds {{vote:m5}}, and then approved the amended by-law {{vote:m6}}. If Council adopts it, the change takes effect January 1, 2024. It would let the Region remove people from its premises or issue fines.

The committee backed the Paramedic Services 2024 pre-budget request for service enhancements {{vote:m4}}. It also recommended a COCHI-OPHI housing investment plan that includes two new staff positions {{vote:m3}}. It received reports on the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness and on affordable housing incentives, including parking requirements.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that Council declare intimate partner violence and violence against women an epidemic, ask the Province to do likewise, and make it a separate priority in the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan.
The committee recommended amending By-law 13-050 to prohibit harassing and discriminatory behaviour on Regional premises, as set out in Appendix A of the report.
The committee recommended amending the proposed by-law to include socio-economic and housing status among the grounds covered.
The committee recommended approving the service enhancements requested for January 1, 2024 in report PHP-PSV-23-006.

The committee recommended approving the investment plan for submission to the Province and two new fully funded staff positions, and asking the Province for more Canada-Ontario Housing Benefit funding for households experiencing homelessness.

debate: One councillor worried that calling intimate partner violence an epidemic might normalize it, as with COVID or the flu. Delegates replied that it was already normalized and the label says it is common but must change. Another councillor said an epidemic declaration is meant to direct resources to the problem.

Delegates said the declaration costs nothing, and said prevention programs rely heavily on donations and only partly subsidized provincial funding. Staff said adding intimate partner violence to the Community Safety and Wellbeing Plan would go to the steering committee this fall.

Delegates supporting the Code of Use amendment said hate incidents that fall short of crimes are not addressed elsewhere, and that the Region should act rather than only state intent. A councillor proposed adding socio-economic and housing status, and legal staff saw no legal obstacle.

On the Plan to End Chronic Homelessness, one councillor said the report felt hopeless given limited Regional finances and called for more provincial and federal help. Another asked for winter recommendations before the 2024 budget, and others asked for updates on addictions and on refugees and asylum seekers.

On affordable housing incentives, township councillors said many of the tools do not fit their communities, which lack transit and surplus land and already waive development charges. A Cambridge councillor said the parking study ignored vehicle and driveway sizes for large families.
